√वच् (adādi, 2P), liṭ (perfect), prathama-puruṣa bahuvacana, parasmaipada

sandhi.note: -āḥ before a vowel: the ru becomes y, the y is dropped, and the two vowels stand apart (देवा | ऊचुः) without further joining.

morph.note: Perfect plural of √वच्: in the weak forms the root takes samprasāraṇa (वच् → उच्), and the reduplicating उ + उच् gives ऊच्: ऊचुः ‘they said’. Compare the singular उवाच (4.28).

mantras.anvaya_en: Subject and verb: a speaker label.

comm.t: The gods answer the Goddess’s offer of a boon (4.32). Their reply runs to 4.37, the last speech of the Madhyama Carita before Medhas closes the story.

words.en: by the Blessed One — by you
words.g: f. instr. sg. of भगवती; agent of the passive कृतम्; the respectful third person used for ‘you’
past passive participle (kta) of √कृ (tanādi, 8U ‘to do’), n. nom. sg.; predicate of सर्वम्
n. nom. sg. of सर्व; subject
indeclinable (negative particle)
indefinite pronoun: किम् (n. nom. sg.) + the particle चित्; with न, ‘nothing’
अव + √शिष् (rudhādi, 7P ‘to leave’), karmaṇi form, laṭ (present), prathama-puruṣa ekavacana, ātmanepada

sandhi.note: Final m before a consonant becomes anusvāra, twice.
Final t becomes d before a vowel.

morph.note: Passive of अव + √शिष् ‘to leave’ (stem शिष्य- with yak): ‘is left’, used in the intransitive sense ‘remains’.
Instrumental of भगवती, the feminine of भगवत् (भग + matup, ‘possessing fortune’). Speaking of the person addressed in the third person is a mark of reverence.

mantras.anvaya: भगवत्या सर्वं कृतम्; किंचित् न अवशिष्यते।
mantras.anvaya_en: Two short clauses: a passive statement with the agent in the instrumental (भगवत्या … कृतम्), then a negated present.
mantras.lit: Everything has been done by the Blessed One; nothing at all remains.
mantras.tr: You, Blessed One, have done everything; nothing is left to be done.
mantras.tr_note: The respectful third person भगवत्या is turned into the second person ‘you’.

comm.t: A half-verse. The gods’ first answer is that they need nothing more: what they asked for has been accomplished. The reason is given in the next line (4.35): Mahiṣa is dead.
A modern reading: the gods begin by declaring themselves content before they ask anything, and when they do ask, it is for protection and for others (4.36–37).

words.g: indeclinable use of the relative यद् (conjunction ‘that, because’); gives the reason for 4.34
demonstrative pronoun इदम्, m. nom. sg.; qualifies महिषासुरः

sandhi.note: Final t becomes d before a vowel; the m of अयम् becomes anusvāra before n (मोऽनुस्वारः, 8.3.23).
Before the sibilant ś the visarga of निहतः may stand unchanged (an optional rule; the alternative would be निहतश्शत्रुः). After u and before a vowel the ru of शत्रुः stays r: शत्रुरस्माकम्.

sandhi.split: च + अपि + वरः + देयः + त्वया + अस्माकम्
sandhi.note: a + a → ā (चापि) and ā + a → ā (त्वयास्माकम्); -aḥ before the voiced d → -o (वरो); visarga before t → s (देयस्त्वया).

samasa.literal: the asura who is Mahiṣa (the buffalo)
samasa.alt: Also analysed as a madhyamapadalopī karmadhāraya, महिषरूपः असुरः, ‘the asura in buffalo form’; the sense is the same.

samasa.sense: Supreme Ruler — the feminine of Śiva’s title Maheśvara
samasa.alt: महत् takes the form महा- as the first member of a karmadhāraya, then महा + ईश्वरी → महेश्वरी.

morph.note: नि + √हन् + kta: the root’s nasal is lost before -ta (हत): ‘struck down, slain’.
Gerundive of √दा with the kṛtya affix yat; the ā becomes e before it: देय, ‘to be given’. With the agent in the instrumental (त्वया) it forms an impersonal ‘must/should be given by you’.
The genitive plural appears twice: first possessive (‘our enemy’), then for the recipient (‘to us’), where classical prose would often use the dative.

mantras.anvaya: यत् अयम् अस्माकं शत्रुः महिषासुरः निहतः, (अतः सर्वं कृतम्)। (हे) महेश्वरि, यदि च अपि त्वया अस्माकं वरः देयः, (4.36 …)
mantras.anvaya_en: The first line is a causal clause (यत् … निहतः) explaining 4.34. The second line is a conditional (यदि …) whose main clause comes in 4.36: ‘if a boon is still to be given, (then) …’.
mantras.lit: in that this Mahiṣāsura, our enemy, has been slain. And if even so a boon is to be given to us by you, O Great Sovereign, —
mantras.tr: for Mahiṣāsura, our enemy, lies slain. Yet if you would still grant us a boon, O Supreme Sovereign, —
mantras.tr_note: The gerundive ‘is to be given by you’ is rendered ‘if you would grant’; the sentence continues in 4.36.

comm.t: The first line gives the reason for 4.34: the enemy who drove the gods from heaven (2.1–8) is dead. The second line turns, politely and conditionally, to the request; the boon itself is named in 4.36–37.
महेश्वरी, the feminine of Maheśvara, Śiva’s title, names the Goddess as sovereign in her own right. The gods’ courtesy — ‘if a boon is still to be given’ — is the tone in which the text has them ask.

f. voc. sg. of अमलानना; compound (see Samāsa)

sandhi.note: Visarga before c becomes s, and the s becomes the palatal ś next to the palatal c.
After ai and before a vowel the ru stays r (स्तवैरेभिः); after i and before t the visarga becomes s (एभिस्त्वाम्).
Final i before the unlike vowel a becomes y.
a + ā → ā; likewise अमल + आनने → अमलानने.

samasa.vigraha: परमाः च ताः आपदः च, ताः
अमलम् आननं यस्याः सा, तत्सम्बुद्धौ (अमल = न विद्यते मलं यस्य तत्)
samasa.type: bahuvrīhi (its first member अमल is itself a nañ-bahuvrīhi)
samasa.literal: she whose face is without stain
samasa.sense: O Goddess of the spotless, radiant face

morph.note: Repetition of a word (āmreḍita) expresses ‘again and again, every time’: संस्मृता संस्मृता, ‘remembered each time’. The participle has a conditional force: ‘(when) remembered’.

Optative in -ethāḥ (stem in -a + -īthāḥ), the ātmanepada ending, from a root classically conjugated in the seventh class and parasmaipada (optative हिंस्याः). Such forms are common in epic and Purāṇic Sanskrit (ārṣa). Compare भवेथाः in 4.37.
Simple future of √स्तु: guṇa of u (स्तो-) + -sya-, with s becoming ṣ after o: स्तोष्यति. √स्तु is aniṭ, so no connecting -i-.

mantras.anvaya: (हे) अमलानने, संस्मृता संस्मृता त्वं नः परमापदः हिंसेथाः। यः च मर्त्यः एभिः स्तवैः त्वां स्तोष्यति, (4.37 तस्य …)
mantras.anvaya_en: The first line is the main clause of the conditional begun in 4.35 (‘if a boon is to be given, may you destroy …’). The second line opens a relative clause (यः …) whose correlative तस्य comes in 4.37.
mantras.lit: Remembered, remembered, may you destroy our gravest calamities; and whatever mortal will praise you with these hymns, O you of stainless face, —
mantras.tr: whenever we call you to mind, destroy our worst calamities. And whoever among mortals praises you with these hymns, O Goddess of the stainless face, —
mantras.tr_note: The repeated participle is rendered ‘whenever we call you to mind’; the sentence of the second line continues in 4.37.

comm.t: The gods ask two boons. The first is for themselves: that the Goddess, whenever remembered, should destroy their gravest calamities. The second, begun here and completed in 4.37, is for any human being who praises her with ‘these hymns’, the hymn of 4.2–27.

With these two verses the hymn acquires its fruit (phala) for later reciters. The Goddess herself confirms the promise at length in chapter 12, the Phalastuti, which opens in almost the same words: एभिः स्तवैश्च मां नित्यं स्तोष्यते यः समाहितः (12.2).
A modern reading: the gods, once rescued, ask for help not only for themselves but for every person who will ever say their words. Gratitude turns into intercession.

words.g: pronoun तद्, m. gen. sg.; correlative of यः in 4.36; depends on धनदारादिसम्पदाम्
m. instr. pl.; compound (see Samāsa); instrumental of respect with वृद्धये (‘increase in …’)

words.en: of his possessions — riches, wife and the rest
words.g: f. gen. pl.; compound (see Samāsa); depends on वृद्धये
f. dat. sg. of वृद्धि (√वृध् + ktin); dative of purpose
f. nom. sg.; compound (see Samāsa); qualifies त्वम्
युष्मद्, nom. sg.; subject of भवेथाः

indeclinable (adverb of time: सर्व + -dā)
f. voc. sg. of अम्बिका

sandhi.note: a + ṛ → ar: vitta + ṛddhi → vittarddhi.
After ai and before the voiced dh the ru stays r.
Final e before initial a: the a is absorbed (avagraha). Inside the compound the d of अस्मद् is unvoiced before p (खरि च, 8.4.55).
ā + a → ā; the same inside the compound धनदार + आदि → धनदारादि.

samasa.vigraha: वित्तं च ऋद्धिः च विभवः च, तैः
धनं च दाराः च धनदाराः (itaretara dvandva); धनदाराः आदयः यासां ताः धनदारादयः (bahuvrīhi); धनदारादयः च ताः सम्पदः च, तासाम् (karmadhāraya)
samasa.type: karmadhāraya containing a bahuvrīhi in आदि, which contains a dvandva
samasa.literal: of the possessions that begin with wealth and wife
samasa.sense: of his riches, his wife and family, and all he has
samasa.alt: Also possible as a ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa, धनदारादीनां सम्पदः, ‘the prosperity of his wealth, wife and the rest’; the sense differs little.

samasa.sense: favourable to the gods who ask
samasa.alt: अस्मत् could also be read as a separate ablative plural, ‘pleased (by our praise) from us’; the printed text joins it, and ‘gracious to us’ is the natural sense.

morph.note: Optative of √भू with the ātmanepada ending -ethāḥ; classical Sanskrit uses only the parasmaipada (भवेः). Like हिंसेथाः in 4.36, an epic (ārṣa) form, perhaps chosen for the metre.
Dative of वृद्धि expressing purpose (tādarthya): ‘for the growth of …’.
The suffix -dā forms adverbs of time from pronouns: सर्वदा ‘at all times’, यदा, तदा, कदा.

mantras.anvaya: (हे) अम्बिके, अस्मत्प्रसन्ना त्वं सर्वदा तस्य वित्तर्द्धिविभवैः धनदारादिसम्पदां वृद्धये भवेथाः।
mantras.anvaya_en: The main clause of the relative sentence begun in 4.36 (यः … स्तोष्यति — तस्य …). The genitive तस्य goes with धनदारादिसम्पदाम्; the instrumental वित्तर्द्धिविभवैः is loosely attached, best taken as ‘in respect of wealth …’ with वृद्धये.
mantras.lit: for the increase of his possessions — riches, wife and the rest — in wealth, prosperity and splendour, may you, gracious to us, always be (present), O Ambikā.
mantras.tr: may you, O Mother, ever gracious to us, be with that person always, to increase his wealth, prosperity and fortune, his riches, his wife and family, and all he has.
mantras.tr_note: The loose instrumental and the genitive are rendered together as a list of what increases; ‘be with that person’ makes explicit the sense of भवेथाः … वृद्धये, ‘be (there) for the increase’.

comm.t: The second boon, completed: whoever recites ‘these hymns’ should be granted increase in every worldly good — wealth, prosperity, splendour, riches, wife and household. The gods ask the Goddess to be always gracious to them, and so to him.

The two boons together — protection from calamity when remembered (4.36) and prosperity for the reciter (4.37) — are the fruits the tradition attaches to the Śakrādi stuti. They are the first statement in the text of the reward of recitation, set out in full by the Goddess in chapter 12.
A modern reading: the text does not separate devotion from ordinary life. Wealth, home and family are asked for openly, as things the Goddess is glad to increase.

flags.uncertain: The construction of the instrumental वित्तर्द्धिविभवैः is loose: it may go with वृद्धये (‘increase in wealth …’) or be read as a list parallel to धनदारादिसम्पदाम्. The meaning is the same either way; the reading of the text is not in doubt.
